claim: Collective migration is a directed, coordinated motion of many self-propelled agents.
source: Collective migration—the directed, coordinated motion of many self-propelled agents—is a fascinating emergent behavior exhibited by active matter with functional implications for biological systems.
evidence: This is a definitional statement presented in the abstract that establishes the concept being studied.

claim: Bacterial populations autonomously smooth out large-scale perturbations in their overall morphology.
source: We find that bacterial populations autonomously smooth out large-scale perturbations in their overall morphology, enabling the cells to continue to migrate together.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study supported by experimental observations and simulations.

claim: The smoothing process arises from spatial variations in the ability of cells to sense and respond to the local nutrient gradient.
source: This smoothing process arises from spatial variations in the ability of cells to sense and respond to the local nutrient gradient—revealing a population-scale consequence of the manner in which individual cells transduce external signals.
evidence: This is a mechanistic finding derived from analysis of experimental and simulation data.

claim: Collective migration enables populations to follow cues that would be undetectable to isolated individuals.
source: In addition to being a fascinating example of emergent behavior, collective migration can be critically important—enabling populations to follow cues that would be undetectable to isolated individuals (Camley, 2018), escape from harmful conditions and colonize new terrain (Cremer et al., 2019), and coexist (Gude et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Collective migration enables populations to escape from harmful conditions and colonize new terrain.
source: In addition to being a fascinating example of emergent behavior, collective migration can be critically important—enabling populations to follow cues that would be undetectable to isolated individuals (Camley, 2018), escape from harmful conditions and colonize new terrain (Cremer et al., 2019), and coexist (Gude et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Perturbations can be external, stemming from heterogeneities in the environment.
source: These can be external, stemming from heterogeneities in the environment (Sándor et al., 2017; Morin et al., 2016; Wong et al., 2014; Chepizhko and Peruani, 2013; Chepizhko et al., 2013; Chepizhko and Peruani, 2015; Toner et al., 2018; Maitra, 2020), or internal, stemming from differences in the behavior of individuals (Yllanes et al., 2017; Bera and Sood, 2020; Alirezaeizanjani et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Perturbations can be internal, stemming from differences in the behavior of individuals.
source: These can be external, stemming from heterogeneities in the environment (Sándor et al., 2017; Morin et al., 2016; Wong et al., 2014; Chepizhko and Peruani, 2013; Chepizhko et al., 2013; Chepizhko and Peruani, 2015; Toner et al., 2018; Maitra, 2020), or internal, stemming from differences in the behavior of individuals (Yllanes et al., 2017; Bera and Sood, 2020; Alirezaeizanjani et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: In some cases, perturbations can abolish coordinated motion throughout the population entirely.
source: Indeed, in some cases, perturbations can abolish coordinated motion throughout the population entirely (Sándor et al., 2017; Morin et al., 2016; Yllanes et al., 2017; Bera and Sood, 2020; Chepizhko and Peruani, 2013; Chepizhko et al., 2013; Chepizhko and Peruani, 2015; Toner et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Perturbations can couple to the active motion of the population to destabilize its leading edge, producing large-scale disruptions to its morphology.
source: In other cases, perturbations couple to the active motion of the population to destabilize its leading edge, producing large-scale disruptions to its morphology (Wong et al., 2014; Alert and Trepat, 2020; Alert et al., 2019; Driscoll et al., 2016; Doostmohammadi et al., 2016; Williamson and Salbreux, 2018; Miles et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Morphological instabilities can occur due to the disruptive influence of hydrodynamic interactions between cells during chemotaxis.
source: Indeed, for one of the simplest cases of collective migration—via chemotaxis, the biased motion of cells up a chemical gradient—morphological instabilities can occur due to the disruptive influence of hydrodynamic (Subramanian et al., 2011; Lushi et al., 2012; Lushi et al., 2018) or chemical-mediated (Ben Amar and Bianca, 2016; Ben Amar, 2016; Funaki et al., 2006; Brenner et al., 1998; Mimura and Tsujikawa, 1996; Stark, 2018) interactions between cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Morphological instabilities can occur due to the disruptive influence of chemical-mediated interactions between cells during chemotaxis.
source: Indeed, for one of the simplest cases of collective migration—via chemotaxis, the biased motion of cells up a chemical gradient—morphological instabilities can occur due to the disruptive influence of hydrodynamic (Subramanian et al., 2011; Lushi et al., 2012; Lushi et al., 2018) or chemical-mediated (Ben Amar and Bianca, 2016; Ben Amar, 2016; Funaki et al., 2006; Brenner et al., 1998; Mimura and Tsujikawa, 1996; Stark, 2018) interactions between cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Mechanisms by which migrating populations can withstand perturbations have scarcely been examined.
source: By contrast, mechanisms by which migrating populations can withstand perturbations have scarcely been examined.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field that identifies a knowledge gap.

claim: Chemotaxis in response to a self-generated nutrient gradient provides both the driving force for collective migration and the primary smoothing mechanism for bacterial populations.
source: We show that chemotaxis in response to a self-generated nutrient gradient provides both the driving force for collective migration and the primary smoothing mechanism for these bacterial populations.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study supported by experimental and simulation data.

claim: The limited ability of cells to sense and respond to a nutrient gradient causes them to migrate at different velocities at different positions along a front.
source: Furthermore, using continuum simulations, we show that the limited ability of cells to sense and respond to a nutrient gradient causes them to migrate at different velocities at different positions along a front—ultimately driving smoothing of the overall population and enabling continued collective migration.
evidence: This is a mechanistic finding derived from continuum simulations.

claim: Differential migration velocities ultimately drive smoothing of the overall population and enable continued collective migration.
source: Furthermore, using continuum simulations, we show that the limited ability of cells to sense and respond to a nutrient gradient causes them to migrate at different velocities at different positions along a front—ultimately driving smoothing of the overall population and enabling continued collective migration.
evidence: This is a mechanistic finding derived from continuum simulations.

claim: The hydrogel particles are swollen in a defined rich liquid medium with L-serine as the primary nutrient and chemoattractant.
source: The media are composed of hydrogel particles that are swollen in a defined rich liquid medium with L-serine as the primary nutrient and chemoattractant.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental setup.

claim: The hydrogel is highly swollen and freely permeable to oxygen and nutrient.
source: Because the hydrogel is highly swollen, it is freely permeable to oxygen and nutrient.
evidence: This is a property of the experimental system established by the authors.

claim: Cells cannot penetrate the individual hydrogel particles and are instead forced to swim through the interparticle pores.
source: However, while the particles do not hinder exposure of bacteria to these chemical signals, the cells cannot penetrate the individual particles and are instead forced to swim through the interparticle pores (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental system supported by the schematic in Figure 1B.

claim: Varying the hydrogel particle packing density enables tuning of pore size and thereby modulates cellular migration without altering the nutrient field.
source: Varying the hydrogel particle packing density thus enables us to tune pore size and thereby modulate cellular migration without altering the nutrient field (Bhattacharjee and Datta, 2019a; Bhattacharjee and Datta, 2019b; Bhattacharjee et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a methodological capability supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Each undulated cylinder requires approximately 10 seconds to print.
source: Each undulated cylinder requires ∼10 s to print, two orders of magnitude shorter than the duration between successive 3D confocal image stacks, ∼10 min.
evidence: This is a measurement of the experimental procedure stated in the figure caption.

claim: The duration between successive 3D confocal image stacks is approximately 10 minutes.
source: Each undulated cylinder requires ∼10 s to print, two orders of magnitude shorter than the duration between successive 3D confocal image stacks, ∼10 min.
evidence: This is a measurement of the experimental procedure stated in the figure caption.

claim: Cells of E. coli initially 3D-printed in densely packed straight cylinders collectively migrate radially outward in smooth, coherent fronts.
source: For example, as we showed previously (Bhattacharjee et al., 2021), cells of E. coli initially 3D-printed in densely packed straight cylinders collectively migrate radially outward in smooth ('flat'), coherent fronts.
evidence: This is a finding from previous work by the authors.

claim: These fronts form and propagate via chemotaxis.
source: These fronts form and propagate via chemotaxis: the cells continually consume surrounding nutrient, generating a local gradient that they in turn bias their motion along (Adler, 1966; Cremer et al., 2019; Fu et al., 2018; Saragosti et al., 2011; Bai et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a mechanistic explanation supported by citations to previous work.

claim: In the absence of nutrient, migrating fronts do not form at all.
source: In the absence of nutrient, migrating fronts do not form at all (Bhattacharjee et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a finding from previous work by the authors.

claim: The outer periphery of the population spreads slowly after 3D printing, hindered by cell-cell collisions in the pore space.
source: After 3D printing, the outer periphery of the population spreads slowly, hindered by cell-cell collisions in the pore space, as the population establishes a steep gradient of nutrient through consumption (Bhattacharjee et al., 2021).
evidence: This is an observation from the experiments supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The periphery spontaneously organizes into an approximately 300 μm-wide front of cells that collectively migrates outward.
source: Then, this periphery spontaneously organizes into an ∼300 μm-wide front of cells that collectively migrates outward (yellow in Figure 1C).
evidence: This is an observation from the experiments shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The front autonomously smooths out large-scale undulations as it continues to propagate.
source: Strikingly, however, the front autonomously smooths out these large-scale undulations as it continues to propagate (Video 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experiments shown in Video 1.

claim: The smoothing of collective migration is regulated by both the undulation wavelength and the ease with which cells migrate.
source: Our experiments thus indicate that the smoothing of collective migration is regulated by both the undulation wavelength and the ease with which cells migrate.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Variants of the Keller-Segel model can successfully capture the key features of chemotactic migration of flat E. coli fronts in bulk liquid.
source: Variants of this model can successfully capture the key features of chemotactic migration of flat E. coli fronts in bulk liquid (Keller and Segel, 1971; Fu et al., 2018) and in porous media (Bhattacharjee et al., 2021); we therefore hypothesize that it can also help identify the essential physics of smoothing.
evidence: This is a statement about previous work supported by citations.

claim: Variants of the Keller-Segel model can successfully capture the key features of chemotactic migration of flat E. coli fronts in porous media.
source: Variants of this model can successfully capture the key features of chemotactic migration of flat E. coli fronts in bulk liquid (Keller and Segel, 1971; Fu et al., 2018) and in porous media (Bhattacharjee et al., 2021); we therefore hypothesize that it can also help identify the essential physics of smoothing.
evidence: This is a statement about previous work supported by citations.

claim: The continuum Keller-Segel model recapitulates the essential spatio-temporal features of smoothing seen in the experiments.
source: This agreement confirms that the continuum Keller–Segel model recapitulates the essential spatio-temporal features of smoothing seen in the experiments.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing simulations to experiments.

claim: The simulated fronts form, collectively migrate, and smooth in a manner that is remarkably similar to the experiments.
source: Although we do not expect perfect quantitative agreement between the experiments and simulations due to their difference in dimensionality and the simplified treatment of cell-cell interactions, the simulated fronts form, collectively migrate, and smooth in a manner that is remarkably similar to the experiments.
evidence: This is a comparison between simulation and experimental results.

claim: In the simulations, the normalized undulation amplitude decays exponentially over time, as in the experiments.
source: Similar to the experiments, the outer periphery of each population first spreads slowly, then spontaneously organizes into an outward-migrating front that eventually smooths. We again find that the normalized undulation amplitude decays exponentially over time, as shown in Figure 2D.
evidence: This is a finding from the simulation data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Differential proliferation typically destabilizes bacterial communities.
source: However, differential proliferation typically destabilizes bacterial communities, as shown previously both experimentally and theoretically (Fujikawa and Matsushita, 1989; Bonachela et al., 2011; Nadell et al., 2010; Farrell et al., 2013; Trinschek et al., 2018; Allen and Waclaw, 2019).
evidence: This is a statement about previous work supported by citations.

claim: Chemotaxis is both necessary and sufficient for the observed front smoothing.
source: Therefore, chemotaxis is both necessary and sufficient for the observed front smoothing.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the simulation results in Figure 3.

claim: Variations in the local nutrient gradient along the leading edge of the front do not contribute to smoothing; rather, they oppose it.
source: This spatial variation in the driving force promotes faster outward chemotactic migration at the peaks than at the valleys, amplifying front undulations—in opposition to our observation that the migrating population self-smooths. Variations in the local nutrient gradient along the leading edge of the front do not contribute to smoothing; rather, they oppose it.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the analysis of the simulation data.

claim: Because high nutrient concentrations saturate cell-surface receptors, the chemotactic response function decreases with nutrient concentration.
source: That is, because high nutrient concentrations saturate cell-surface receptors, the chemotactic response function decreases with nutrient concentration.
evidence: This is a mechanistic explanation based on established knowledge of receptor saturation.

claim: Nutrient concentrations are larger at the peaks than at the valleys along the leading edge of the front.
source: Inspection of the nutrient field indicates that nutrient concentrations are larger at the peaks than at the valleys along the leading edge of the front (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is an observation from the simulation shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The chemotactic response of cells is weaker at peaks than at valleys.
source: Thus, the chemotactic response of cells is weaker at peaks than at valleys, as shown by the points in Figure 4B, yielding slower outward chemotactic migration at peaks than at valleys and thereby reducing the amplitude of front undulations.
evidence: This is a finding from the simulation data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Variations in the chemotactic response along the leading edge of the front promote smoothing.
source: Variations in the chemotactic response along the leading edge of the front promote smoothing, unlike variations in the nutrient gradient.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the analysis of the simulation data.

claim: The robustness of the front morphology to perturbations has never been examined or quantitatively explained.
source: The smoothing of these fronts underlies the utility of standard agar-based assays for chemotaxis, in which bacteria spread outward in smooth, circular rings from a dense inoculum (Wolfe and Berg, 1989; Tittsler and Sandholzer, 1936; Croze et al., 2011; Cremer et al., 2019)—despite the presence of irregularities in the initial inoculum that are inevitably introduced by human error. To our knowledge, the robustness of the front morphology to such perturbations has never been examined or quantitatively explained; as a result, previous studies have only focused on the migration of the smooth fronts that ultimately result (Adler, 1966; Lauffenburger, 1991; Keller and Segel, 1971; Cremer et al., 2019; Fu et al., 2018; Saragosti et al., 2011; Bhattacharjee et al., 2021; Bai et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field that identifies a knowledge gap.

claim: The work provides an explanation for why perturbed fronts smooth out.
source: Our work now provides an explanation for why perturbed fronts smooth out.
evidence: This is a summary of the contribution of the study.

claim: The 3D printing platform provides a unique way to tune the shape of the initial perturbation, as well as the extent to which cellular migration is hindered.
source: The 3D printing platform provides a unique way to tune the shape of the initial perturbation, as well as the extent to which cellular migration is hindered.
evidence: This is a statement about the methodological contribution of the study.

claim: Even though cells in peaks of an undulated front experience a stronger driving force given by the local nutrient gradient, the higher nutrient levels they are exposed to saturate their cell-surface receptors, and hence they exhibit a weaker chemotactic response than cells in valleys.
source: We find that even though cells in peaks of an undulated front experience a stronger driving force given by the local nutrient gradient, the higher nutrient levels they are exposed to saturate their cell-surface receptors, and hence they exhibit a weaker chemotactic response than cells in valleys.
evidence: This is a mechanistic finding from the study.

claim: While variations in the nutrient gradient along the leading edge of a front act to amplify undulations, variations in the ability of cells to sense and respond to this gradient dominate and instead smooth out the undulation.
source: That is, while variations in the nutrient gradient along the leading edge of a front act to amplify undulations, variations in the ability of cells to sense and respond to this gradient dominate and instead smooth out the undulation.
evidence: This is a mechanistic finding from the study.

claim: The mechanism of smoothing is distinct from diffusion, which is typically responsible for the smoothing of traveling waves in reaction-diffusion systems.
source: Importantly, this mechanism of smoothing is distinct from diffusion, which is typically responsible for the smoothing of traveling waves in reaction-diffusion systems—and in our case, is much too slow to drive smoothing.
evidence: This is a comparison to other known mechanisms.

claim: The second requirement for chemotactic smoothing is satisfied for diverse active matter systems.
source: The second requirement is also satisfied for diverse active matter systems; in the context of chemotaxis, specific examples include other bacteria (Menolascina et al., 2017), enzymes (Jee et al., 2018; Agudo-Canalejo et al., 2018; Mohajerani et al., 2018), aggregating amoeba cells (Keller and Segel, 1970), and mammalian cell groups during development, immune response, and disease (Camley, 2018; Iglesias and Devreotes, 2008; Theveneau et al., 2010; McLennan et al., 2012; Malet-Engra et al., 2015; Puliafito et al., 2015; Tweedy et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a generalization supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The chemotactic smoothing process is autonomous, arising without any external intervention.
source: The chemotactic smoothing process described here is autonomous, arising without any external intervention.
evidence: This is a characterization of the phenomenon observed in the study.

claim: Chemotactic smoothing is a population-scale consequence of the limitations in cellular signal transduction.
source: Instead, it is a population-scale consequence of the limitations in cellular signal transduction—motivating future studies of other population-scale effects, beyond smoothing, that may emerge from individual behaviors.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the mechanistic findings of the study.

claim: The work highlights the distinct and pivotal role played by the cellular chemotactic response function in regulating migration and large-scale population morphology.
source: Indeed, while studies of chemotaxis typically focus on the role of the external nutrient gradient in driving cellular migration, our work highlights the distinct and pivotal role played by the cellular chemotactic response function in regulating migration and large-scale population morphology more broadly.
evidence: This is a summary of the contribution of the study.

claim: The work contributes a new factor to be considered in descriptions of morphogenesis.
source: Our work therefore contributes a new factor to be considered in descriptions of morphogenesis, which thus far have focused on the role of other factors—such as differential forcing by signaling gradients, differential proliferation, intercellular mechanics, substrate interactions, and osmotic stresses (McLennan et al., 2012; Fujikawa and Matsushita, 1989; Bonachela et al., 2011; Nadell et al., 2010; Farrell et al., 2013; Trinschek et al., 2018; Allen and Waclaw, 2019; Beroz et al., 2018; Fei et al., 2020; Yan et al., 2019; Yan et al., 2017; Copenhagen et al., 2020; Smith et al., 2017; Ghosh et al., 2015; Zhang et al., 2021)—in regulating the overall morphology of cellular communities and active matter in general.
evidence: This is a summary of the contribution of the study supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The liquid medium was an aqueous solution of 10× MOPS Mixture, 10× ACGU solution, 5× Supplement EZ solution, 20% glucose solution, 0.132 M potassium phosphate dibasic solution, and ultrapure Milli-Q water at volume fractions of 10, 10, 20, 1, 1, and 58%, respectively.
source: The components to prepare the EZ Rich were purchased from Teknova Inc, autoclaved prior to use, and were mixed following the manufacturer's directions; specifically, the liquid medium was an aqueous solution of 10× MOPS Mixture (M2101), 10× ACGU solution (M2103), 5× Supplement EZ solution (M2104), 20% glucose solution (G0520), 0.132 M potassium phosphate dibasic solution (M2102), and ultrapure Milli-Q water at volume fractions of 10, 10, 20, 1, 1, and 58%, respectively.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental preparation.

claim: The hydrogel granules swell considerably, resulting in a jammed medium made of approximately 5–10 μm diameter swollen hydrogel particles with approximately 20% polydispersity.
source: The hydrogel granules swell considerably, resulting in a jammed medium made of ∼5–10 μm diameter swollen hydrogel particles with ∼20% polydispersity and with an individual mesh size of ∼40–100 nm, as we established previously (Bhattacharjee and Datta, 2019b), which enables small molecules (e.g., amino acids, glucose, oxygen) to freely diffuse throughout the medium.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental system supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The individual mesh size of the swollen hydrogel particles is approximately 40–100 nm.
source: The hydrogel granules swell considerably, resulting in a jammed medium made of ∼5–10 μm diameter swollen hydrogel particles with ∼20% polydispersity and with an individual mesh size of ∼40–100 nm, as we established previously (Bhattacharjee and Datta, 2019b), which enables small molecules (e.g., amino acids, glucose, oxygen) to freely diffuse throughout the medium.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental system supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The mesh size of the swollen hydrogel particles enables small molecules (e.g., amino acids, glucose, oxygen) to freely diffuse throughout the medium.
source: The hydrogel granules swell considerably, resulting in a jammed medium made of ∼5–10 μm diameter swollen hydrogel particles with ∼20% polydispersity and with an individual mesh size of ∼40–100 nm, as we established previously (Bhattacharjee and Datta, 2019b), which enables small molecules (e.g., amino acids, glucose, oxygen) to freely diffuse throughout the medium.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental system supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The 3D printing process does not appreciably alter the properties of the hydrogel packing and is sufficiently gentle to maintain the viability and motility of the cells.
source: Moreover, as we showed in our previous work Bhattacharjee et al., 2021, this process does not appreciably alter the properties of the hydrogel packing and is sufficiently gentle to maintain the viability and motility of the cells.
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental method supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The confocal images only show the actively moving cells near the leading edge of each propagating front because it is exposed to sufficient oxygen for the GFP to properly fold.
source: We note that because our experiments probe fluorescence from GFP-expressing cells, the confocal images only show the actively moving cells near the leading edge of each propagating front because it is exposed to sufficient oxygen for the GFP to properly fold.
evidence: This is an explanation of the experimental observations.

claim: Under oxygen-depleted conditions, the GFP expressed by the cells does not properly fold, and the cells lose fluorescence over approximately 30 minutes.
source: As these cells move outward, they continually consume nutrient and oxygen—eventually causing the trailing 'inner' region of the population to become oxygen-depleted, as shown in our previous work (Bhattacharjee et al., 2021). Under these conditions, we conjecture that the GFP expressed by the cells does not properly fold, and the cells lose fluorescence over ∼30 min.
evidence: This is a conjecture based on observations and previous work.

claim: E. coli consume L-serine first.
source: E. coli consume this amino acid first (Yang et al., 2015) and respond to it most strongly as a chemoattractant compared to other components of the media (Wong et al., 2014; Mesibov and Adler, 1972; Adler, 1966; Menolascina et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a statement about E. coli behavior supported by citations.

claim: E. coli respond to L-serine most strongly as a chemoattractant compared to other components of the media.
source: E. coli consume this amino acid first (Yang et al., 2015) and respond to it most strongly as a chemoattractant compared to other components of the media (Wong et al., 2014; Mesibov and Adler, 1972; Adler, 1966; Menolascina et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a statement about E. coli behavior supported by citations.

claim: The pore space is too small to fit multiple cells side-by-side in the experiments.
source: Indeed, our porous media are highly confining; the pore sizes are <8 μm, comparable to the size of a single-cell body (length ∼2 μm and width ∼0.5 μm) and its flagella (length ∼5 μm), in all cases. Hence, because the pore space is too small to fit multiple cells side-by-side, cell-cell interactions are necessarily restricted to end-on interactions.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental system.

claim: Cell-cell interactions are necessarily restricted to end-on interactions in the experiments.
source: Hence, because the pore space is too small to fit multiple cells side-by-side, cell-cell interactions are necessarily restricted to end-on interactions. We directly confirmed this phenomenon experimentally in our prior study (Bhattacharjee et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental system supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Radial and out-of-plane effects do not need to be considered to capture the essential features of bacterial front formation and migration.
source: While the experimental geometry is three dimensional, in previous work (Bhattacharjee et al., 2021), we found that radial and out-of-plane effects do not need to be considered to capture the essential features of bacterial front formation and migration.
evidence: This is a finding from previous work by the authors that justifies the 2D modeling approach.

claim: Smoothing appears to be robust to large changes in the environmental conditions.
source: Smoothing therefore appears to be robust to large changes in the environmental conditions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the parameter exploration.
